source_ref.authors: Joshi AM, Raveendran AV, Arumugam M
source_ref.title: Therapeutic role of yoga in hypertension
source_ref.section: PRECAUTIONS AND CONTRAINDICATIONS; Table 3 kumbhaka row

evidence.locus: World J Methodol 2024;14(1):90127, precautions prose and Table 3 kumbhaka row (PMC10989416, accessed 2026-08-26).
evidence.paraphrase: This medical review discusses yoga practices in hypertension. In the precautions section it writes that practicing kumbhaka (breath retention) during pranayama can raise systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial pressure, citing Nivethitha 2017, and that kumbhaka is contraindicated in hypertension, heart disease, and individuals recovering from an illness, surgery, or injury. Table 3's kumbhaka cell reports the blood-pressure rise; the prose writes 'contraindicated'. Those two speech acts stay unmerged in this record. The review does not name box breathing or square breathing. Yoga-as-treatment claims, ujjayi without retention, and the adjacent bandha / long-retention sentence are out of scope for this record. A general line that people with health problems should seek medical opinion before yoga is a general yoga precaution, not a hold-specific who-list for the four-phase candidate.
evidence.population: stated as people with hypertension, heart disease, or recovering from illness, surgery, or injury, in a yoga-for-hypertension review; not a box/square clinical population

observed_exclusions.condition: recovering from an illness, surgery, or injury

observed_physiology.as_source_writes: authors cite Nivethitha 2017 for an acute rise; this is a citation, not an independent measurement in this review

transfer_limits: kumbhaka is not four-phase square breathing
unspecified or long retention is not a short timed hold
review exclusion of kumbhaka is not a who_must_not_hold list for the four-phase candidate
Table 3 physiology cell is not the same speech act as the prose contraindication
adjacent bandha or long-retention sentence is a different named practice
general yoga consult-first is not hold-specific

source_ref.authors: Nivethitha L, Mooventhan A, Manjunath NK
source_ref.title: A pilot study on evaluating cardiovascular functions during the practice of Bahir Kumbhaka (external breath retention)

evidence.locus: Adv Integr Med 2017;4:7–9, legally readable abstract and publisher-visible methods/results (accessed 2026-08-26). Full PDF not required for this record. Hold duration is not stated in this locus.
evidence.paraphrase: This pilot reports cardiovascular measures during bahir kumbhaka, which the paper names as external breath retention after exhalation, distinct from antar kumbhaka. Nineteen healthy volunteers (mean age about 23.5 years) from a South Indian university were studied; people with systemic or mental illness, regular medication, or chronic smoking or alcoholism were excluded from the sample. During the practice the authors report a significant rise in systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial pressure. In this study systolic pressure reverted after the practice; diastolic pressure and mean arterial pressure did not. The authors attribute the systolic rise to higher heart rate / cardiac output together with higher total peripheral resistance. The paper does not list populations who must not hold the breath. It does not name box breathing or square breathing. Hold duration is not stated in this legally readable locus and is not imported from other papers by the same authors. Absence of serious adverse effects in this healthy sample is not a product clearance.
evidence.population: nineteen healthy volunteers, mean age 23.53 (SD 3.08), university sample in South India; not a hypertensive or box/square clinical population
transfer_limits: empty-lung retention is physiologically closer to a post-exhale hold but is not the product dose
unspecified retention in this locus is not a short timed hold
study response is not a contraindication
healthy-volunteer acute response is not a population exclusion list
do not import hold duration from other Nivethitha papers
no serious adverse effects in this sample is not product clearance
